explanation:
OBSERVATION: At 390x844 both pages lay the note's

out the same way: 4 lines, 280x80 at y=552–632. On second-a the containing div#shipping-info.notice (the yellow box, background rgb(255,248,225)) is 60px tall at both viewports. At 1440x900 the text needs only 2 lines (40px), so 60px is enough. At 390x844 the box ends at y=602, while the text runs to y=632. In hit-testing below y=602 the

is missing from the stack entirely (selfDepth = -1); it is not merely covered by something. The next element in flow, the 'Weiter zur Zahlung' button, starts at y=610, inside the region where the text's 4th line would be. On second-b the notice grows to 100px at 390x844, the

is topmost at every in-rect sample point, and every row has text ink. EXPLANATION (inferred, not read directly): second-a gives the notice a fixed height of about 60px and clips its overflow, probably with overflow:hidden. When the sentence wraps to 4 lines on a phone, it is cut at y=602. That boundary falls inside the 3rd line box (592–612), so the reader sees the sentence end partway through a line, which matches the report. second-b lets the box grow with its content (auto height). H1 (vertical clipping) is supported for second-a and rejected for second-b. H2 (horizontal overflow) is rejected on both. H3 (occlusion) is rejected as the primary cause: the button only appears in the area the clipped text would have used, and the

is not in the stack beneath it.

unsupportedOrUntested: The exact CSS (height:60px / max-height plus overflow:hidden) is inferred from geometry and hit-testing. The broker does not expose overflow, height or max-height.

Clipping by overflow is inferred because the

is missing from elementsFromPoint stacks inside its own rect. A 'pointer-events:none' on the clipped part or a clip-path would show the same hit-test result, but those would not move the button upward.
I did not view the screenshot artifacts. Reading the pixel cells as 'button fill' rests on p50=81 matching the button background rgb(47,93,58) in greyscale and on the hit-test result.

observations.statement: The sentence is fully in the DOM, opaque and visible, and identical on both pages at both viewports.
No horizontal overflow on either page; the text wraps normally to 4 lines at 390px.
On desktop both pages look the same and nothing is clipped, which matches 'on the laptop it seems fine'.

On second-a at 390px, the 3rd line is partly visible: there is ink in row 2 (y 592–612), but the hit-test at y=602 already falls outside the box. This means the cut runs through the middle of a line box, matching 'cut off in the middle of a line'.

contradictions.description: Second-a row 2 (y 592–612) has p05 = 81 in cols 0–1, whereas second-b has 72/59. This probably mixes the clipped upper half of line 3 with the top of the button (from y=610) or the notice's bottom edge. It fits clipping but was not resolved per pixel row.

Measurement harness mismatch: the probe ignored packet.viewport and opened both viewports itself, so each page@viewport record holds identical duplicate runs. Artifact ids in the '@1440x900' records are also labelled 1440x900 for the 390px run. This does not change the data, but each viewport effectively has one independent sample.
citations: second-a@390x844: runs[1] identical to second-a@1440x900: runs[1]

contradictions.description: The low ink in row 1 col 2 at 1440 and row 2 col 2 at 390 appears on both pages. It is probably the ragged end of a line, not part of the defect.

uncertainties.question: Is the clipping caused by height:60px + overflow:hidden on .notice, by max-height, or by line-clamp-like styling?
uncertainties.whyNotResolvable: The broker returns only a fixed subset of computed styles, without height, max-height or overflow.
uncertainties.nextMeasurement: Inspect the computed style of div#shipping-info.notice in devtools, or check that the fixed height scales with the viewport by testing an intermediate width.
